body:
## Severity: P2 (downgraded from filed P0)

## Context

R1 audit originally flagged P0 because the resend path could theoretically resend a different message than the one that failed. On re-audit it's P2 because the failure window is narrow (template versions rarely change mid-flight) but the design is still wrong and will eventually bite.

## Finding

`EmailService.resendFailed()` matches the failed message to the resend by recipient + subject + first 200 chars of body rather than by the message's persisted UUID. If the email template is updated between the original send-attempt and the resend (e.g., a deploy lands in the resend window), the body-match fails and either:

- (a) nothing resends (silent loss), or
- (b) a stale template body is used instead of the current one.

## Fix sketch

Persist a `message_id` (UUID) on the original send attempt, store it in the failure queue, and look up by ID on resend. Template version stays correct because the body is regenerated from `template_id` + payload at resend time, not copied.

## Acceptance

Resend path looks up by UUID; template change between send and resend produces the correct new-template body; no silent drops.

## Source

R1 audit (backend), P0→P2 downgrade in verdict file. See `p0_claims_audit_report.md` referenced in `HANDOFF_OP_50.md`.

## Origin

Filed as part of the Operator-49 → Operator-50 R81-backfill P2 batch (backend track). See `handoffs/quality-bar-raise/current-state.json` `session_findings_to_file[R1-P0-7]` for telemetry pointer.
title: [P2] Failed-email resend uses fuzzy body-match instead of message ID — risk of resending wrong message after template change
